'''''Leucadendron strobilinum''''', commonly called the '''peninsula conebush''', is a plant species in the genus ''[[Leucadendron]]''—forming part of the family [[Proteaceae]]. Confined to the [[Cape Peninsula]] of [[South Africa]], it reaches a height of up to {{convert|2.6|m}} growing in southern, damp rocky slopes at an elevation of 500 to 1100m.<ref name=rebelo>{{cite book |last1=Rebelo |first1=Tony |title=Sasol Proteas: A Field Guide to the Proteas of Southern Africa |date=1995 |publisher=Fernwood Press |isbn=1-874950-02-4 |page=200}}</ref> Its conservation status is [[Near Threatened]]—a result of inappropriate fire management, fire-break clearing and alien plant invasions.<ref name="iucn status 17 November 2021" />

==Appearance==
A large, single-stemmed shrub reaching a height of up to 2.6m.<ref name=rebelo/> It branches near the base and has dark-green elliptical leaves.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Manning |first1=John |title=Field Guide to Fynbos |date=2018 |publisher=Struik Nature |location=Cape Town |isbn=978-1-77584-590-4 |page=260 |edition=2}}</ref>

==Ecology==
As with all [[leucadendron]], the peninsula conebush is [[dioecious]]. Flowering takes place between September and October, with flowers described as yeast scented.<ref name=rebelo/> Seeds are stored on the (female) plant, an adaptation known as [[serotiny]], to be released upon a fire occurring; the seeds are winged allowing for wind dispersal.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tyambetyu |first1=Olivia |title=Leucadendron strobilinum |url=http://pza.sanbi.org/leucadendron-strobilinum |website=PlantZAfrica.com |publisher=South African National Biodiversity Institute (SANBI) |access-date=11 November 2019}}</ref>
